newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower on late profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower on late profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Tuesday as late profit-taking erased earlier gains triggered by Wall Street's sharp overnight rise. Brokers said the market likely was easing into a consolidation.
The weighted index, which had remained moderately higher for most of the session, tailed off in late trade to finish 23.26 points or 0.27 percent lower at 8,616.11.
Turnover was a heavy T$171.12 billion.
Despite a Wall Street-induced 2.91 percent rise in closely watched electronics, the overall index could not fend off what brokers called technical resistance at its new higher levels.
"There just wasn't enough momentum to push the index past the 8,700 level, which is widely seen as a big resistance level," said Chen Han-chung, analyst for Yungli Securities.
"The market will likely stay put at the current level in the foreseable future," Chen added.
The heavily weighted financials, which has been one of the hottest sectors in the market's 25 percent 1997 rally, lost 2.04 percent on Tuesday.
Fubon Insurance dropped 3.51 percent or T$3 to close at T$82.50.
Brokers said the index likely would consolidate until the run-up to the one-year anniversary of President Lee Teng-hui's inauguration as Taiwan's first directly elected leader on May 20.
"Investors widely expect that the government is not going to allow the market to have another sharp fall on May 20 like last year," said Oliver Fang, analyst for National Securities.
The volatile market had put a damper on Lee's big day in 1996 by plummeting 246.29 points.
A 8,550-8,650 range was seen for Wednesday.
